case_name: Jagdish Kumar & Anr v. State Of H.P And Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: State of H.P and anr (wife's parents-in-law, brother-in-law, etc.)

acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Informant married Yaman Thakur in 2015. Husband became cruel after one month, abused and beat her. Parents-in-law assisted him. Dowry demands made. Informant's parents-in-law, sister-in-law, and brother-in-law gave beatings on 26.04.2022.

legal_principles.principle: A complaint can be quashed where the allegations made in the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out the case alleged against the accused.
legal_principles.held: The principles relating to the exercise of jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to quash complaints and criminal proceedings have been stated and reiterated by this Court in several decisions.
cited_cases: Indian Oil Corporation v. NEPC India Limited (2006) 6 SCC 736
A.M. Mohan v. State, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 339
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — relevant to exercise of jurisdiction under Section 482

legal_principles.principle: A complaint may also be quashed where it is a clear abuse of the process of the court, as when the criminal proceeding is found to have been initiated with mala fides/malice for wreaking vengeance or to cause harm, or where the allegations are absurd and inherently improbable.
legal_principles.held: The principles relating to the exercise of jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure to quash complaints and criminal proceedings have been stated and reiterated by this Court in several decisions.
cited_cases: Indian Oil Corporation v. NEPC India Limited (2006) 6 SCC 736
A.M. Mohan v. State, 2024 SCC OnLine SC 339
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — relevant to exercise of jurisdiction under Section 482

legal_principles.principle: The power to quash shall not, however, be used to stifle or scuttle a legitimate prosecution. The power should be used sparingly and with abundant caution.

legal_principles.principle: A complaint is not required to verbatim reproduce the legal ingredients of the offence alleged. If the necessary factual foundation is laid in the complaint, merely on the ground that a few ingredients have not been stated in detail, the proceedings should not be quashed.
